issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary of a trust may be joined as a proper party to a suit for specific performance concerning the trustees’ proposed sale of trust property.
material_facts: Trustees entered into an agreement to sell trust property to the plaintiff, who sued for specific performance after the trustees did not complete the sale.

The applicant sought to join the suit as a beneficiary of the trust, alleging that the proposed sale price was substantially below the property’s value and that the sale could prejudice the beneficiaries.
The trial court allowed the applicant to be joined, but the High Court reversed that order.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiary was a proper party and could be impleaded. The appeal was allowed, and the trial court’s order adding the beneficiary as a defendant was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order I Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a court may add a proper party whose presence would enable it to completely, effectively, and adequately adjudicate the matters in dispute. A beneficiary is not a stranger to a dispute concerning the trustees’ alienation of trust property, since trustees must act reasonably in exercising their power of alienation under the trust. The Court applied the principles discussed in Mumbai International Airport (P) Ltd. v. Regency Convention Centre & Hotels (P) Ltd., including its discussion of Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.applicant_is_trust_beneficiary: The person seeking to join the suit is a beneficiary of the trust that owns the property.
predicates.suit_concerns_trustee_sale_of_trust_prop: The suit concerns an agreement by trustees to sell property belonging to the trust.
predicates.beneficiary_may_be_added_as_proper_party: The beneficiary may be added to the suit as a proper party.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks specific performance of an agreement by trustees to sell trust property, a beneficiary of that trust may be added as a proper party.
